limitations: An idealized vertical throw; real balls feel drag.
title: Zero velocity at the top, but is acceleration zero?
story:
Mia tosses a ball straight up and watches it climb, slow down, and stop for an instant at the top. "It's not moving there," she says, "so nothing is acting on it. Acceleration must be zero."

Is she right? Acceleration is not how fast the ball moves. It is how fast its velocity changes. On the way up the velocity is positive and shrinking. On the way down it is negative and growing in size. Every second, the velocity drops by about 9.8 m/s, whether the ball goes up, stops or comes down.

Take a throw at 5 m/s. After 0.25 s the velocity is about 2.5 m/s. After 0.51 s it is zero. After 0.76 s it is about -2.5 m/s. The velocity changes by the same amount in each equal step, and it passes through zero without pausing its change.

So at the top the velocity is zero but the acceleration is still -9.8 m/s^2, pointing down. If gravity switched off there, the ball would hang in the air. It does not, because gravity is still pulling. The ball is still for an instant only because its velocity is changing sign. Zero velocity does not mean zero acceleration.
cardDescription: At the top of a throw the ball is still for an instant, so $v=0$. But gravity keeps pulling, so the acceleration stays $-g$. Velocity is zero; acceleration is not.
instructions: Press Play and watch the arrows. Drag the scrubber or press At top to stop at the highest point. Change the launch speed and compare again.
learningGoal: Say that gravity still pulls the ball down at the top of its throw, where it is still for an instant.

scene.description: One moving ball on a fixed height scale with a launch-height guide; the scale does not change with the launch speed, so a faster toss visibly rises higher. A blue Motion arrow beside the ball shortens on the way up, is absent at the top and points down on the way back. A separate dashed warm gravity arrow keeps the same direction and length throughout. Beside the ball a callout (frame object id callout.toss) names the motion and shows gravity. The scene starts at launch and runs the whole rise and fall. No second ball, graph, equation, number readout or comparison strip.

entities.label: Ball
entities.purpose: The tossed ball (frame object id ball.toss), an SVG glyph that starts at the launch mark.

entities.label: Motion arrow
entities.purpose: Blue arrow showing the signed velocity (frame object id vec.v, labelled v); absent at the top.

entities.label: Gravity arrow
entities.purpose: Dashed warm arrow (frame object id vec.a, labelled a), the same downward length throughout.

entities.label: Launch-height guide
entities.purpose: A fixed guide at the launch height on one height scale.

quantities.label: Launch speed
quantities.meaning: Upward speed at the instant of the throw.
quantities.reference: Measured at the launch mark, up is positive.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Magnitude of the constant downward acceleration.

quantities.label: Time of the top
quantities.meaning: Elapsed time from launch at which the velocity is zero.

quantities.label: Height of the top
quantities.meaning: Height of the ball at its top above the ground mark.
quantities.reference: Measured from the ground mark, up is positive.

quantities.label: Vertical velocity
quantities.meaning: Signed rate of change of height, up positive; zero at the top.

quantities.label: Height of the ball
quantities.meaning: Height above the ground mark, up positive; the launch height is its value at t = 0.
quantities.reference: Measured from the ground mark, up is positive.

quantities.label: Vertical acceleration
quantities.meaning: Signed rate of change of velocity: constant and negative (down), -gravity.

observations.text: The Motion arrow shortens while the ball rises, is absent at the top and points down while it falls.
The gravity arrow keeps the same direction and length, so gravity pulls down at the top too.
A faster toss reaches its top later and higher on the same fixed height scale.

checkpoints.label: Rising
checkpoints.expected: Moving up: a short blue Motion arrow up, gravity arrow down.

checkpoints.label: At the top
checkpoints.expected: Still for an instant at the top: no Motion arrow, gravity arrow still down; playback pauses here.

checkpoints.label: Falling
checkpoints.expected: Moving down: a short blue Motion arrow down, gravity arrow down.

checkpoints.label: Fastest toss at its top
checkpoints.expected: At the fastest launch speed the top comes later and higher on the same height scale.

mode.initialState: Launch speed 5 m/s; the ball at the launch mark, 1.5 m above the ground mark, time 0.000 s, paused.

controls.label: Play
controls.purpose: Run the motion and replay it.
controls.selectionReason: Time explains the change, and the one supported transport drives every linked view.

controls.label: Time since launch
controls.purpose: Inspect any instant of the motion.
controls.selectionReason: A scrubber lets the learner stop on the instants the explanation compares.

controls.label: Launch speed
controls.purpose: See how the speed of the toss moves the top without changing what gravity does there.
controls.selectionReason: The speed varies continuously and intermediate speeds show that the top moves while the pull does not; two named cases would hide that.

controls.label: At top
controls.purpose: Jump to the top of the toss and pause there.
controls.selectionReason: The top is the one instant the explanation is about; a button reaches it exactly, which dragging the scrubber does not.
controls.effect: Seeks the top marker and pauses.

controls.label: Reset experiment
controls.selectionReason: Replay keeps the settings; Reset restores them so the learner can start over.
controls.effect: Restores launch speed 5 m/s and time 0, paused.

claims.text: At the top the velocity is zero and the acceleration is still downward, so gravity keeps pulling.
claims.check: Differentiate v = u - g t: the slope is -g at every t, including the top.

assumptions: Gravity fixed at 9.8 m/s^2, no air resistance, up is positive.
